title: Why everyone agrees in the meeting and disagrees after
series: The invisible rules of human behavior

scenes.say: You stay quiet. You see others stay quiet. So you assume they all agree. Psychologists call this pluralistic ignorance.
Then the real views show up later, in the private chat after the meeting.
In Asch's classic line studies, about three in four people went along with a clearly wrong group answer at least once. Alone, almost nobody got it wrong.

data.title: Clear line-length task
data.footer: Group answers were planted and wrong

scenes.say: At work, one interview study found most employees recalled staying silent about a concern, often to avoid being seen negatively.
Next meeting, it may help to ask, what would make this fail? Send this to the colleague who only disagrees in the chat.

data.text: Who in your meeting is quietly disagreeing?
data.kicker: Send to the colleague who disagrees in the DM
